title: Adaptive triage heuristic for pricing & billing requests across commitment lifecycles, invoicing exceptions, and marketplace offsets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Incoming non-bug customer requests related to pricing, commitments, invoicing exceptions, and marketplace credits are triaged ad hoc across teams. That creates inconsistent decisions, delayed resolution, revenue leakage, and misallocated credits. Goal: Provide a lightweight, repeatable triage heuristic + intake template that Product, Support, Sales, and Finance can use to route/prioritize requests and produce deterministic outcomes (approve, deny, defer, escalate, finance-adjust). Scope: Hosted API commitments, reserved Dedicated capacity adjustments, marketplace credit offsets, one-off invoice adjustments, and cost allocation tagging. Not in scope: technical bugs, legal negotiations, or long-form bespoke enterprise contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form fields capture required signals (issuer, customer tier, revenue impact estimate, contractual reference, urgency, compliance flags).
Scoring rubric implemented in a triage sheet and sample automation rules for 'auto-approve low-risk, low-dollar' cases.
Escalation matrix documented (Support -> PM -> Finance -> Legal) with SLA for each step.
Three example tickets processed end-to-end with correct routing, labels, and resolution artifacts (PR/Confluence/Invoice entry).
Stakeholder sign-off from Support, Sales Ops, and Finance recorded.

example_routing_rules: Auto-approve: Revenue impact < $250, customer_tier = 'self-serve', no contract references, compliance_flag = false -> Support auto-resolve and tag as 'billing-auto' (24h SLA).
PM-review: Revenue impact between $250 and $5,000 or dedicated capacity adjustments that don't change contract duration -> Route to PM queue for 3-day SLA review.
Finance-approval: Any retroactive invoice credit request or commitment change referencing contract ID -> Route to Finance with mandatory doc attachments and 5-business-day SLA.
Escalate-to-legal: Any request with data residency/PII or regulatory compliance flags -> Pause automated flows, assign to Legal and PM for approval.
scoring_rubric: Signals collected: estimated_monthly_revenue_impact, customer_lifetime_value_tier, number_of_affected_endpoints_or_teams, engineering_effort_points, compliance_risk_boolean.
Default weights: estimated_monthly_revenue_impact=40, customer_lifetime_value_tier=25, number_of_affected_endpoints_or_teams=15, engineering_effort_points=10, compliance_risk=10.
Score bands: 0-30 = Low (auto-resolve candidate), 31-65 = Medium (PM review), 66-100 = High (Finance/Leadership).
Example: $1,200 monthly impact for mid-market (tier 3), 1 endpoint affected, 3 engineering points, no compliance risk -> weighted score = 52 -> PM review.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Keep intake minimal to encourage submission vs collect more signals to avoid back-and-forth. Decision: adopt 7 mandatory fields + 3 recommended fields.
Automate low-dollar adjustments to reduce manual effort but require audit trail to satisfy finance. Decision: auto-approve threshold set conservatively at $250 initially.
Scoring complexity vs adoption. Decision: provide both 'quick mode' (5 signals) and 'detailed mode' (full rubric) in intake.
Implementation approach: prefer Zendesk + Google Sheet + GitHub actions over building new internal UI in Q2 to hit short-term SLAs.
